title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Still Here Fest - Beloved Asheville Benefit
location: NC, United States
description: Still Here Fest is a celebration of the resilience of the Western North Carolina community. After the horrific events of Hurricane Helene, cities like Asheville and many others in the region saw firsthand the power and the strength of love and empathy. Spearheading the relief efforts, groups like Beloved Asheville and so many others dropped everything to serve, care for, and feed their community, neighbors, friends, and strangers alike. At the front of many of these relief efforts were the artists and musicians, putting aside their creative drive to take time to bring food, water, and other life-saving supplies to those in need. Still Here Fest 2026 is in recognition of not only the efforts of these groups and individuals but also the resilient spirit of Western North Carolina. We survive, we thrive, we are still here.

description:
Saturday, September 26, 2026 7:00 PM | Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Outdoor Stage | From $40.83 adv. Event Details & Tickets
Sunday, September 27 | Doors: 2 pm | Show: 3 pm | From $40.83 adv. Event Details & Tickets

Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. All the while, the band has cultivated a devoted grassroots following traveling to communities big and small by train, horseback, bio-diesel bus and sailboat.


Sisters Leah Song and Chloe Smith were raised in Atlanta in a blue collar bohemian family. Their mom was a fiddler, their dad a sculptor. They went to contra dances, wandered the neighborhood forests and had a childhood filled with banjos, harmony singing and other folkways. In her early twenties, while studying art and Indigenous activism in Chiapas, Mexico, Leah returned to her love of folk music. The two sisters then began a wildly creative and successful career that has included busking in New Orleans, traveling with a circus from Southern Italy to Northern Sweden, and collecting songs in Ireland, Bulgaria and Colombia. Rising Appalachia also features the creative musicianship of Duncan Wickel (fiddle, cello), David Brown (upright bass, baritone guitar) and Biko Casini (drums, percussion) — each tradition keepers in their own right.

location: Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain, 2948 US-70, Black Mountain, NC, 28711
description:
September 19, 2026 7:30 PM | Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Outdoor Stage | $36.15 adv. Event Details and Tickets 
  
After spearheading the alt-country movement with Uncle Tupelo, Jay Farrar pursued his vision with Son Volt, who recorded three landmark albums in the ’90s before the groundbreaking artist put the band on extended hiatus and cut three solo LPs. Missing the free exchange of ideas and the surprises that inevitably occur when a group of simpatico musicians lock together, Farrar assembled a new lineup of Son Volt in 2004 and has since released nine albums. The latest album, Sound Signal Serenades, was released as a special 2026 Record Store Day limited edition LP. Jay Farrar’s work often seeks out the ghosts of America’s discordant or forgotten past, converses at length with them, and writes songs that stake a claim to a better future. 
  
Shannon McNally
At home across the American (Americana) music spectrum, the Grammy nominee who’s live music career began on the jam band circuit of the 1990’s with bands like Derek
Trucks and Railroad Earth, writes as well as she interprets the songs of others, has a top tier musicality to her craft, a soul stirring, honest and at times elegant voice that
immediately grabs one by the heart strings and a troubadour’s wanderlust, not to mention as it turns out, she is also an excellent electric guitar player.

title: Biltmore Estate: Walk the Westover Black Trails
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Located at The Inn on Biltmore Estate, the Westover Black Trails provide access to some of Biltmore's beautiful woodlands. We will loop the Black Trail in a counterclockwise direction.

Biltmore says it is 3.5 miles. The Black Trail is narrow. It is a moderately difficult trail. There is elevation change, but just a bit strenuous. (For those who have walked the Green and Blue Trails, there is less chance for confusion.)

When you drive to the Inn, you will turn onto its access road. Near the entrance to the Inn is the entrance to the parking area. There are two rows of parking, an upper row closer to the Inn, and a lower row a little further from the Inn. We will gather on the lower row at the far end (away from the Inn).

If you need a restroom prior to the walk, Antler Hill is very close and there are public restrooms there. No restroom facilities are available during the walk.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case you will want light hiking boots. Walking sticks are desirable; I plan to use two. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome if they are accustomed to trail walking. Trail strollers would find this a bit difficult.

There is a grounds admission fee. We walk at Biltmore several times each year, so an annual grounds pass is highly recommended.

Many regular Biltmore guests have never walked the Westover Trails. I think you will enjoy these.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

Each fall, the last monarch butterflies of the year pass through Western North Carolina on their incredible migration to Mexico. Join us on Saturday, September 19, for a day dedicated to celebrating monarchs, pollinators, and the communities that connect us to the outdoors.

title: The Art of Wellbeing: Therapeutic Art Making in the Museum
location: NC
description:
Art has the power to heal, restore, and reconnect us to what matters most. Join us at the Asheville Art Museum for a guided art-making session led by a registered art therapist, designed to explore how art can be a tool to nurture your mental and emotional wellbeing. Whether you’re a seasoned artist or have never picked up a paintbrush, come as you are and leave feeling refreshed. Join Alexis for sessions on August 15, September 19, and December 19. 
Dr. C. Alexis Decosimo is a licensed mental health clinician, registered art therapist, and Doctor of Public Health. She specializes in helping children, families, and individuals access healing through blending therapeutic artmaking and evidence-based approaches including EMDR, cognitive behavioral therapy, and person-centered approaches.
She believes in meeting clients where they are, drawing on creative modalities to open pathways to healing that talk therapy alone may not reach. Her clinical work is deeply informed by over a decade of international experience building mental health programs in some of the world’s most under-resourced settings, giving her a grounded, adaptive, and culturally sensitive approach to care.
In her Asheville practice, she brings that same commitment to accessible, ethical, and community-rooted mental health support to help clients process trauma, build resilience, and find their footing through the power of expressive therapy.   For more information follow: Ashevillearttherapy.com 
Purchase Tickets 
Please enter through the Staff Entrance to the left of the building.

title: The Southern Highland Craft Guild's 46th Annual Heritage Weekend
location: Folk Art Center, Blue Ridge Parkway
description:
You are invited to our 46th. annual Heritage Weekend on September 19 and 20 at the Folk Art Center on the Blue Ridge Parkway. 
Many of you have been to this fun event in the past and we will again host over 20 heritage artist, musicians and dancers to honor and celebrate Mountain Heritage Crafts. 
One of the highlights of the celebration is our Annual World Gee Haw Whimmy Diddle competition on Saturday afternoon. 
A Whimmy Diddle is an Appalachian mountain toy, traditionally made from 2 sticks  of rhododendron. Notches are carved into the stick and a propeller is attached to the end. Rubbing the notches with the second stick makes the propeller spin! The trick is to make it spin gee (to the right) or haw (to the left). 
Contestants are judged by their skills and interesting prizes will be awarded. 
The music stage will provide entertainment with Blue Grass and Gospel music, and cloggers will demonstrate the mountain dance tradition.

Come for the craft, stay for the music!

title: Reptiles of Western North Carolina
description:
Reptiles of Western North Carolina
with Carlton Burke 
Saturday, September 19  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
  
The Southern Appalachian Mountain region hosts an interesting combination of cold-blooded reptiles, based largely on various factors such as the diverse mountain elevations and the unique forest and other habitat types. Species here range from the endangered and threatened Bog Turtle and Timber Rattlesnake to more common species such as the Black Rat Snake and Northern Fence Lizard. Participants in this class will learn about the various reptile species in western North Carolina, their life cycles and habitats, and threats and conservation efforts in place to protect them. In addition, some live mountain reptiles will be joining us as special guests. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Book + Art | Fiction and Photos of Appalachia
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
September’s Book + Art lecture features an author and artist couple, Stephanie and Jeff Whetstone. Stephanie will speak about her debut novel Deep Belly of the Earth a haunting, intimate story of friendship, marriage, motherhood and the fierce pull of home set in a Kentucky coal mining community, while her husband Jeff Whetstone, Professor of Photography at Princeton, will speak about his latest collection of photographs of Appalachia, including the one on the cover of Deep Belly of the Earth. 
SYNOPSIS of Deep Belly of the Earth
Ava Maynard makes the difficult decision to leave her small coal mining town in Eastern Kentucky to make a life for herself and her son, Joshua, in the city. Her husband, Collis, won’t leave the mountains, even though he has been laid off from his job as a miner. When tragedy strikes, Ava reluctantly slips back into her spot in this troubled world, relying on her deepest friendships to guide her. 
Author Bio
Stephanie Whetstone earned her BA at Duke and her MFA in Creative Writing from UNC-Greensboro, where she was Fiction Editor of the Greensboro Review. She has been a fellow at Virginia Center for the Creative Arts and Hambidge, and a Peter Taylor Scholar at the Sewanee Writer’s Conference. Her fiction has appeared in Tulip Tree Review, Waccamaw, Waypoints, Drafthorse, the Anthology of Appalachian Writers, and Narrative. A native of Kentucky, she now lives in Brooklyn. 
Jeff Whetstone imagines rural America through the lenses of mythology and biology. Whetstone’s work has been exhibited internationally and has received reviews in ArtForum, Art in America, the New York Times, the New Yorker, and the Los Angeles Times. Whetstone earned his MFA from the Yale School of Photography in 2001, where he received the George Sakier Prize for Photography. A recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship, as well as a fellowship from the North Carolina Arts Council, his work is in the permanent collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Nasher Museum, the Nelson Atkins Museum, the Cleveland Art Museum, the Yale Art Gallery, the New York Public Library, and the North Carolina Museum of Art. Whetstone is a Professor of the Practice of Art at Princeton University.

description:
Join us for a screening of Minnie Evans: Draw or Die followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, Linda Royal. 
We are also excited that Wayne Evans, the great-grandson of Minnie Evans, who is in the documentary, will be attending the Q&A as well. 
Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit. 
Screening time: 56:10:00 
Film Synopsis: 
The film explores the inspirational life and artistic mastery of visionary artist Minnie Evans through archived
conversations with her friend Nina Howell Starr. 
About the filmmaker: 
Linda Royal (fka Linda Booker) directed, produced, and edited the film festival award-winning
documentaries “STRAWS,” with narration by Tim Robbins, “Bringing It Home,” and “Love Lived on Death
Row.” Her films have reached audiences worldwide through film festivals, educational distribution,
community screenings, corporate offices, and in-flight entertainment. She has partnered with numerous
organizations for grassroots advocacy and impact campaigns. Linda was the Director of Operations for
the Sonoma International Film Festival in 2015-2016. She started By the Brook Productions after receiving
a Certificate in Documentary Studies from Duke University in 2005. Before filmmaking, Linda was an Art
Director and graphic designer for numerous publications in Florida and North Carolina.

description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
description:
Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
with Jenne Sluder 
Tuesday, September 22 |  10 am – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
Set aside a day for quiet reflection and renewal at the North Carolina Arboretum in Asheville, centering themes from the poetry of W.S. Merwin. Calm your mind, refresh your spirit, and relax your body and nervous system with a gentle immersion into mind-body centering practices both indoors and in nature. Expect slow, mindful yoga and qigong, guided meditation, progressive relaxation + sound bath, contemplative readings from W.S. Merwin, and time for personal journaling and quiet time in nature. All mind-body practices will be gentle and accessible, including the choice to do any seated movements or meditations in a chair or on a cushion according to your own body’s needs. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions.

title: Cataloochee Valley ELK (GSMNP)
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
I am going to Cataloochee Valley in the Smoky Mtn Nat'l Pk to explore, picnic and, hopefully, **catch the Elk during their 'rut' bugling.** Up to 16 are welcome to join me.
This event is suitable for non-hikers and “grade school-age” grandchildren.
**Since the storm destroyed much of the valley road, we will park near the church and see how far we can walk into the valley.**
The elk usually overnight in the valley. Usually, by 4-5pm. There is never a guarantee. But, if we get lucky, it's an event not to be missed.
Cataloochee Valley has a historical home, church and barn which we will take time to explore.
**The plan is to arrive early afternoon to give time to explore and 'PICNIC' before the elk 'present' themselves.**
Bring a folding chair, bug spray, camera, water & food.
Hiking NOT required.
**We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!**
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsh_8qxUfDY**
THOSE WHO MIGHT WISH TO DO THIS ‘ON THEIR OWN’ MAY CONTACT ME, via email (see below), FOR EXACT DIRECTIONS. (mid Sep thru-Mid Oct).
Drive time: 1.25 hr/55 mi (one way) Via I-40W to exit 20 (Jonathan Creek) **(SMOKY MTN NATL PK PARKING TAGS REQR’D – I WILL CONTACT DRIVERS WITH THE INFO).**
**\*\*Special Note\*\*:** The last 5 miles of the drive are not suitable for low sedans. It is a switchback climb up a mountain gravel road. Those with excessive fear of height or prone to carsickness will be uncomfortable on this road.
Google Maps: = “Cataloochee Valley – Elk Watching”
Google Maps: = “Palmer Chapel Methodist Church”
**Return Not earlier than: 7:30 PM**
**CARPOOL CONTRIBUTIONS APPRECIATED. $7.00 SUGGESTED**
**DOGS: Since this in in the Smoky Mtn Nat'l Pk; dogs are NOT invited to this event.**
Weather Check: Jonathan Creek, NC
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 3 driver(s). (=11ppl)
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair.
We suggest slightly open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.

title: AYPROS SEPTEMBER Pub Club: New Belgium
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
Few places make a better backdrop for an AYPROS Pub Club than a brewery overlooking the French Broad River.
Join AYPROS on **Tuesday, September 22** for our September Pub Club at **New Belgium Brewing**, where we’ll spend the evening at their riverside Asheville brewery and Liquid Center on Craven Street.
New Belgium has been part of Asheville’s beer scene for a decade, but the setting alone makes it worth another visit. The 18-acre brewery sits along the French Broad River, with a 6,000-square-foot riverside taproom, plenty of indoor and outdoor space, and furniture and design elements created from repurposed materials and work by local artists.
In other words, it is pretty much built for Pub Club.

Whether this is your first AYPROS event or you know half the room already, Pub Club is meant to be easy. Leave the business cards at home. There is no presentation, no agenda and no expectation that you have to work the room. Grab a drink, find a spot by the river, catch up with some familiar faces and introduce yourself to somebody new.

We’ll be there from **5:00 PM - 8:00 PM**, and, as always, Pub Club is come-and-go. Show up when you can and stay as long as you’d like.

Your **first drink is on us**, courtesy of our Pub Club Title Sponsor, **Allen Stahl + Kilbourne (ASK Law)**.

New Belgium will have its lineup of beers and other beverage options available throughout the evening, and **The Smokin’ Onion** is scheduled to be onsite serving its scratch-made, plant-based food for anyone looking to grab dinner.

## What to Expect

* A relaxed, come-and-go evening along the French Broad River
* Your first drink included courtesy of ASK Law
* Additional beverages available for purchase
* Food available for purchase from The Smokin’ Onion
* Indoor and outdoor seating at New Belgium’s Asheville Liquid Center
* Plenty of time to catch up with friends and meet other young professionals
* First-time attendees and people coming on their own are absolutely welcome
* No formal program or speeches

## Schedule

**5:00 PM** \- Check\-in opens\, first drinks and Pub Club begins
**8:00 PM** \- AYPROS Pub Club concludes

## Location

**New Belgium Brewing**
21 Craven Street
Asheville, NC 28806

## Parking

New Belgium offers **street parking near the brewery as well as two onsite parking lots**. Please do not park in the gravel production lot behind the brewery.
Come when you can, find us by the river, grab your first drink and spend an early fall evening with Asheville’s young professional community at one of the city’s best-known brewery destinations.
A special thank you to **New Belgium Brewing** for welcoming AYPROS and to **Allen Stahl + Kilbourne (ASK Law)** for continuing to make Pub Club possible by picking up everyone’s first drink.
We’ll see you by the river.

title: Scenic AVL #3:  Kennilworth
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
This route includes the Kenilworth neighborhood and the historically diverse South Asheville neighborhood. We will stop at a historic church and cemetery, as well as Kenilworth Park and Chiles House. We will go up Reservoir Rd to take in the view and get a workout.

**Rating: Moderate+**
**Distance:** 5 miles
**Elevation:** 670 feet
**Surface:** Road
**Type:** Butterfly Loop
**Pace:** 3 mph on the flats, slower up Reservoir Rd
**Gear:** In winter, please bring a headlamp or flashlight. water, snack, poles for the climb
**Features:** Neighborhood charm Kenilworth, a little history, and views from the top. Not likely to see bears - but we did see one near this route earlier in the spring.
**Dogs:** On leash.
**Cautions:** Maintain normal traffic awareness.
**Route:** [Kenilworth to Reservoir Rd ](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/kenilworth-to-reservoir-road-overlook-d9e74f4?p=-1&sh=ifwm3x).

**Scenic Asheville Series:** There are 9 [hikes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=drivesdk) in the series; hike them all and receive an [attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) for your backpack. Badgers can always attend hikes, even if you are on the waiting list

**On-Time Departure**
I typically have 1 or 2 no-shows on my hikes, so we don't wait for people to arrive.

If you are late, park on Chile's Avenue near [Leah Chile's Park](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZUs81uHukoRMWQuP8?g_st=ac)
and meet us at the historical marker at the top of the park across from Chile's house.

**Guests and Plus Ones**
This is a pretty good hike to bring guests. It is not as tough as some of the hikes in the series, and if someone wants to bail after the first loop, it is easy to find your way back to the cars.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
This activity involves hiking on city streets that may have traffic. Participants are responsible for their safety on streets and trails. The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. In addition, you acknowledge that you agree to the Meetup terms: [https://www.meetup.com/terms](https://www.meetup.com/terms)

description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom
Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. 
Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! 
Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Sapphic Book Club!  - July
description:
Queers to the Front!
Our book club read for September is *Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil* by V.E. Schwab.

*This is a story about hunger.*

**1532\. Santo Domingo de la Calzada\.**
A young girl grows up wild and wily—her beauty is only outmatched by her dreams of escape. But María knows she can only ever be a prize, or a pawn, in the games played by men. When an alluring stranger offers an alternate path, María makes a desperate choice. She vows to have no regrets.

*This is a story about love.*
**1827\. London\.**
A young woman lives an idyllic but cloistered life on her family’s estate, until a moment of forbidden intimacy sees her shipped off to London. Charlotte’s tender heart and seemingly impossible wishes are swept away by an invitation from a beautiful widow—but the price of freedom is higher than she could have imagined.

*This is a story about rage.*
**2019\. Boston\.**
College was supposed to be her chance to be someone new. That’s why Alice moved halfway across the world, leaving her old life behind. But after an out-of-character one-night stand leaves her questioning her past, her present, and her future, Alice throws herself into the hunt for answers . . . and revenge.

***This is a story about life—***
***how it ends, and how it starts.***

title: Long-term Effects of Hurricane Helene on Southern Appalachian Ecosystems
description:
Long-term Effects of Hurricane Helene on Southern Appalachian Ecosystems
with Dan Lazar 
Wednesday, September 23  |  1 pm – 3 pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
It has been two years since hurricane Helene ravaged the ecosystems of Western North Carolina, uprooting trees and causing major flooding along mountain rivers and streams. How have the animals and plants of the affected areas responded to this historic event?  Where do songbirds go to escape hurricane winds?  How can fish and aquatic invertebrates tolerate such massive flooding?  What factors determine which trees are toppled and which survive?  We will investigate the long-term effects of Hurricane Helene on the natural plant and animal communities of Western North Carolina during this illustrated lecture followed by a short walk on Arboretum grounds to observe the ongoing recovery of hurricane-damaged areas. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Sam Knob; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
Darlene will lead to Sam Knob in the Black Balsam area of the BRPwy; Up to 12 of you are welcome.
After a ½ mile walk through the meadow. the climb is just shy of 400 ft. in ½ mile via several switchbacks on the trail. We pass a lush, young forest of mostly northern hardwood trees. There are many roots and rocky areas along the trail.
Lush vegetation grows near rock outcrops beside the trail, including blueberries, strawberries, sedges and grass, mountain laurel, Carolina rhododendron, and countless wildflowers including bluets. The trail will pass beneath some large rock outcrops, which lie just below the summit. We’ll reach a grassy, shrubby saddle between the two high knobs, and a large outcropping of snow white quartz rocks from a grassy meadow.
Difficulty: Trail Tread Condition: Moderately Rough; Constant moderate climb. Rocky.
WE WILL SPEND TIME FOR LUNCH AT THE TOP.
**We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.”**
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4**
**Social ‘hour’ at 9:15 AM. tires roll at 9:30AM**
Distance: 3 mi RT; Accum Ascent: 570 ft; Pace: **1.25mph**
Drive time: 45min/ 23 mi 1-way
Apprx return time: 3 PM
Carpool contributions appreciated. $3.00 suggested
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is ***NOT*** for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Well trained dogs **(you don’t have to yell)** can be 'off-leash'. 'On leash' during the lunch stop. 'On leash' in vicinity of other hike groups. Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
Weather Check:
https://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Black-Balsam-Knob/forecasts/1894
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 2 driver(s) (=8ppl)
We suggest slightly open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.
Waiver: The organizer of this event is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this event. There are certain risks inherent in any outdoor activity. Each participant, by signing up to attend this event, agrees to release from liability the leader(s), Hendo Fun Friends, its Partners, Affiliates, and members for any accident, injury, illness, or personal loss which might occur while participating in this activity or while traveling in any vehicle during this trip. **Each participant further agrees to abide by the rules and regulations concerning safety, to follow instructions of the leader(s), and not to become intentionally separated from the group.** The leader(s) also has the right to use any images collected on this trip for recording on website photo collections.

title: Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
description:
Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
with Mark Dempsey 
Thursday, September 24  |  1 pm – 4 pm 
BREG – Soil Health Core 
Register Here!
  
Come learn about how soil works and how to improve soil health. We will cover the basics of soil, the critical role of organic matter, how to sample soil and interpret a nutrient test, and what actions you can take to make your soil better. Drawing from research and on-farm experience, the class emphasizes practical, science-based strategies for improving soil health, reducing erosion, and building resilient farming systems. 
Mark Dempsey works with the Carolina Farm Stewardship Association as conservation specialist and soil health educator. His background includes more than 15 years of research and education in soil microbiology, no-till farming, cover crops, and sustainable agriculture systems. He teaches practical, science-based approaches to improving soil health, soil function, and long-term farm resilience.

Plant Sale Member Preview
Thursday, September 24
3:00 – 6:00 p.m. 
Shop Arboretum-grown plants before the sale opens to the public!

title: Free Live Music: Jvnk Drawer
description:
Some bands write songs. Jvnk Drawer excavates them
— pulling from a thirty-year vein of half-forgotten gems, salvaged riffs, and songs that were simply waiting for the right band to play them. The result is alternative rock with real mileage on it: melodies sharp enough to catch you off guard, lyrics honest enough to stick. 
At its center is Gavin Conner, a songwriter whose Asheville roots run back to 2007, when he arrived in town to join local favorites, If You Wannas. What followed was a long apprenticeship in the local scene — a solo run, countless stages, and a songbook that quietly grew into something few writers ever amass. By 2017, that songbook needed a band worthy of it, and Jvnk Drawer was born, with drummer Chris Peterson and bassist Erik Avots rounding out the lineup and giving the songs a pulse. 
Like most everything else, the band’s momentum stalled when the pandemic hit, and the members drifted toward other projects to wait it out. But the songs didn’t go anywhere, and neither did the itch to play them. Jvnk Drawer has since reformed sharper and more locked-in than ever, splicing decades of Gavin’s back catalog together with newly written material that sounds like it’s always belonged there. 
The name says it best: a jumble of pieces that when put together, somehow make perfect sense. Equal parts catchy and cutting, Jvnk Drawer is proof that the best songs are worth digging for. 
Gavin Conner — Vocals, Guitar Chris Peterson — Drums Erik Avots — Bass 
  
Free Show 6-8p. All Ages.

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Walking Meditation & Qigong
description:
Walking Meditation & Qigong
with Jenne Sluder 
Friday, September 25  |  9 – 10am 
Register Here!
  
Enjoy a slow, mindful walking meditation through the gardens, practicing breath awareness and sensory attention to touch the deep peace and simple wonders of quiet time in nature. This session begins with a series of gentle and easy Qigong movements to clear the mind, release tension, support the body and brain’s natural healing processes, and generate a sense of inner calm. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?\*\*
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision.](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.

title: Bats of the NC Arboretum with Mist Netting Demonstration
description:
Bats of the NC Arboretum with Mist Netting Demonstration
with Megan Zeger and team 
Friday, September 25  |  7 – 9pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
The NC Arboretum hosts a variety of bat species in our forests. Join a group of biologists for a presentation about the recent acoustic bat study they conducted on the Arboretum’s property this summer and which species they found. Then, once the presentation is over, join the crew out in the woods for a mist netting demonstration if weather allows. During this class, you will learn all about the different species of bats that call the NC Arboretum home, how biologists collect data about bat presence in a location using microphones, and even might have the chance to see live, wild bats up close and personal! 
Participants will not be handling the bats, and the bats will only be handled by the trained biologists. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Megan Zeger is a graduate student at Virginia Tech studying four imperiled bat species in the Asheville, NC area. She has been studying and working with wildlife in the southern Appalachians since 2018 when she started her undergraduate program in wildlife conservation. She has been working with bats since 2022 and has done research on various species in Maryland, North Carolina, Utah, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wyoming. 
Jessica Davey is a wildlife biologist currently working for Virginia Tech’s Conservation and Management Institute. Having graduated from Lees-McRae College in 2021, she has since worked primarily as a bat researcher in six different states. Her experience ranges from Mist netting and acoustic surveys to conducting hibernacula and white-nose swabbing in the caves of Florida. She hopes to continue gaining as much knowledge as she can about the world’s only flying mammal. 
Katie Kadkovsky is a recent Biology graduate from UNC-Chapel Hill. While there, she worked in molecular biology labs at Chapel Hill and Duke studying fungi. Katie was introduced to the bat world at UNC-CH via acoustic surveys of NC’s sky islands. Currently, she is a wildlife biologist with Virginia Tech CMI helping characterize the presence of tri-colored bats in the greater Asheville area to support conservation practices. 
Liam Jawish is a recent graduate from Virginia Tech! He is currently working as a wildlife biologist surveying bats in Asheville, NC. He previously worked on Jaguar surveys in Belize, CA, and bear work in central Virginia. 
Lucy Kraus is a wildlife biologist with the Conservation Management Institute at Virginia Tech. She graduated from UNC-Chapel Hill in 2026 with a degree in environmental science. In the past, she has worked in prescribed fire and environmental education.

title: Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
location: Baker Exhibit Center
description:
Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
September 26, 2026 – January 10, 2027
Baker Exhibit Hall
“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” features Ronan Donovan’s stunning images and videos of wild wolves in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem and Ellesmere Island in the high Canadian Arctic. Since 2014, National Geographic Explorer and photographer Ronan Donovan has examined the relationship between wild wolves and humans in order to better understand the animals, our shared history, and what drives the persistent human-wolf conflict. 
The exhibition, created by National Geographic Society and the National Museum of Wildlife Art, will display images and videos—highlighting the contrast between wolves that live in perceived competition with humans and wolves that live without human intervention.“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” will introduce visitors to the daily lives of wolves in the Arctic—how they hunt, play, travel, and rest in one of the harshest environments on Earth—with unparalleled intimacy. 
About Ronan Donavan
A field biologist turned conservation photographer and filmmaker, Ronan Donovan has explored the human relationship to nature and wildlife on all seven continents. Donovan’s passion for conserving wild animals and wild places was ignited as a child growing up in Vermont and later during his years as a wildlife field biologist researching spotted owls and chimpanzees. He transitioned to visual storytelling as a way to amplify the wildlife researchers and conservationists that Donovan collaborated with. In addition to his National Geographic work on wolves, Donovan has documented human-chimpanzee conflicts in Uganda, and the legacy work of primatologist Dian Fossey focused on mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda. Donovan strives to reconnect viewers to the natural world through the lives of our fellow social mammals to highlight our shared past and interwoven future.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Wellness Day
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Wellness Day at the Asheville Art Museum 
The Asheville Art Museum’s Wellness Day invites visitors to experience the museum as a place for restoration, reflection, creativity, and community. Throughout the day, guests are encouraged to slow down and engage with art through a series of thoughtfully curated wellness experiences that nurture both mind and body. 
Afternoon Tea Parlor | Windgate Foundation Atrium and Plaza noon–4pm 
Yoga on the Plaza | 12:30–1pm 
 Yoga in the Galleries | 1:30–2pm 
Live Music: Soothing sounds in the Galleries and the Windgate Foundation Atrium | noon–4pm 
Drop-in Workshop: Therapeutic Art Making | John & Robyn Horn Education Center (level 3) 1–4pm 
Slow Art Tours | 11:30–noon, 1–1:30pm, 2:30–3pm 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
Museums are uniquely positioned to serve as spaces for wellness. Unlike many public environments, museums invite contemplation, curiosity, and intentional looking. They provide settings where individuals can step away from daily demands and immerse themselves in experiences that inspire wonder, empathy, and personal discovery. Art has the power to help people process emotions, spark meaningful conversations, and connect across diverse perspectives and lived experiences. 
By integrating mindfulness, movement, creative expression, and music into the museum experience, Wellness Day expands the role of the Asheville Art Museum as a community resource dedicated not only to the appreciation of art but also to the holistic well-being of those it serves. The program demonstrates that museums can be active partners in fostering healthier, more connected communities by creating welcoming spaces where creativity becomes a pathway to healing, resilience, and joy.

Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina found here at the NC Arboretum. We will look at using different characteristics including habitat, bark, buds, growth pattern, leaf shape, and fruit/nut shape to identify trees. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

What do we pay when we pay attention?

Ted is interested in anything that can get him out of his head, and music and movement do a pretty good job of that. He hopes to offer music that facilitates an inner journey and invitations that create a shift. While he likes modern electronic music, he can’t create a mix without including lots of natural instruments and voices. Due to a short attention span, he mixes in lots of different musical genres. Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind.

description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
[Get Your Tickets Here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/witchy-ways-day-retreat-tickets-1996341264462)
**Calling in all healers, plant parents, mothers, artists, mystics, rebels, and seekers.**
This day is an invitation to remember and return to all that you are.

Together, we’ll spend an autumn afternoon slowing down, dropping in, and reconnecting with ourselves, the season, and one another through ritual, reflection, movement, and a little witchcraft.

As we move through the energies of fall, we’ll explore the seasonal invitation to both release what has run its course and intentionally call in what we’re ready to cultivate next.

**Flow of the Day**
*We’ll begin by gathering in opening circle, setting our intentions, calling in the directions, and grounding into the space through a guided meditation and energetic release.*

*From there, we’ll move into a ceremonial teaching and transmission, exploring the astrological energies of Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius alongside sacred feminine archetypes that can support us through the shifting season. Guided journaling, shadow reflection, and group sharing will offer space to bring these teachings into your own lived experience.*

*After a nourishing snack break, we’ll return to the body through intentional yoga and movement, creating space for integration and embodiment.*

*We’ll close our time together with a seasonal ritual. A little autumn witchcraft devoted to releasing what you’re ready to leave behind and calling in what you desire to cultivate. Through apple magic, fire, candlelight, and intention, you’ll create a ritual piece to take home and continue tending throughout the season.*

*Our gathering will conclude with a closing prayer and circle, sealing the magic of the day and honoring what has shifted, opened, or been remembered. Snacks and tea will be served.*

**About your guides**
**Jenn (She/Her)** is an intuitive healer trained Yoga Teacher 9+ years, Reiki Master, Astrologer and Spiritual Coach. She combines her knowledge of the body from 13 years working in physical therapy with all spiritual tools that have contributed to her own healing & spiritual journey to help guide others.
**Vi (They/Them)** is a practicing Witch & Psychic who is a trained Yoga Teacher, Reiki Master, and Tarot Reader. They combine their passions of astrology, divination, dance, and creative expression to help others listen to their intuition.
**Alessandra Mary (she/her)** is a ceremonialist, Akashic priestess, mystic, author, and sacred storyteller devoted to the path of remembrance. Through sacred gatherings and oracular transmissions, she weaves soulful experiences that invite you into deeper connection with synchronicity, authenticity, and the unseen magic woven through everyday life. She stewards the land we will be gathering on.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Michelangelo: Love and Death
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Michelangelo – Love and Death offers a cinematic
journey through the great chapels and museums
of Florence, Rome and the Vatican, to the print
and drawing rooms of Europe, to explore
Michelangelo’s tempestuous life. The film goes in
search of a greater understanding of this
charismatic and enigmatic figure, both through
his relationships with his contemporaries and
his ongoing artistic legacy.
The film invites audiences to intimately examine
Michelangelo’s art and artistic process – from the
Carrara quarries where Michelangelo sourced his
marble, to the new technology being used to
attribute works. The film also offers a rare
chance to get up close to the mesmerizing
Rothschild Bronzes, which, following an
extensive research project carried out by
Academics in Cambridge in 2015, were positively
attributed to Michelangelo after over a century of debate.

title: Asheville Foodie Supper Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
🍝 Asheville Foodie Supper Club: First Stop, Italia! 🇮🇹

Sunday, September 27 | 6:00 to 9:00 PM
Strada Italiano | 27 Broadway, Downtown Asheville

Limited to 12 people

I’ve been wanting to create something a little different for Asheville Digital Nomads, something smaller, more intimate, and centered around one of my very favorite ways to bring people together. Food. 😁

So, I’m officially launching the Asheville Foodie Supper Club, a monthly culinary adventure where a small group of us will gather around a table, explore Asheville’s ridiculously good food scene, and actually have time to get to know one another.

We’re kicking this thing off with Italian. 🇮🇹🍝🍷

Our first stop is Strada Italiano in downtown Asheville, a cozy Old World-style trattoria serving regional Italian cuisine inspired by both Northern and Southern Italy. Think house-made pasta, risotto, seafood, Italian classics, good wine, and the kind of food that makes you very happy you did not stay home and eat something responsible. 😆

Each month, we’ll choose a different foodie theme. Italian one month, Korean another, Thai, Indian, Mexican, burgers, pizza, seafood, Mediterranean, tapas, and whatever other interesting culinary rabbit holes we decide to wander down.

But the food is only half the idea. The real purpose of the Asheville Foodie Supper Club is to create a different kind of social experience.

Instead of standing around at a larger event having snippets of conversations with 20 different people, we’ll sit around one table with just 8 to 12 of us. We’ll eat. We’ll talk. We’ll laugh. We’ll hear each other’s stories. We’ll linger over dinner and hopefully turn some of those people we recognize from Meetup into people we actually know.

The intention of this event is to meet interesting people, discover really good food and local restaurants, and enjoy conversations that have enough time to go somewhere.

🍷 A Little Supper Club Fine Print

This event is intentionally limited to 12 people, and unlike some of our larger gatherings, this one requires an actual restaurant reservation.

So please only RSVP if you genuinely intend to come. Don’t grab one of the 12 seats as a “maybe.” If something changes, no problem, just update your RSVP as soon as possible so someone on the waitlist has a chance to join us.

Because when there are only 12 chairs at the table, every chair matters.

Strada also offers a nice range of gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan and dairy-free options, so our first Foodie adventure should have something for just about everyone.

Come hungry and ready to connect with some fun and friendly new humans over a yummy meal together.

Welcome to the Asheville Foodie Supper Club. First stop, Italy. 🇮🇹 🍝🍷🍽️

title: The Morning Read
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**The Morning Read: "Can I afford to … ?"**

...Hire? ....Buy the second van? ....Take the bigger space? ....Raise prices? ....Finally pay myself?

It's the most common question owners ask, and it almost never gets answered — because "afford" isn't a feeling and it isn't the bank balance. It's a number, and it isn't on your P&L.

This session is about learning how to find it. If you're a business owner trying to figure out whether you can afford your next move, or a financial professional with a few tricks up your sleeve for helping folks find the answer faster — come. We'll walk through the numbers that help with decisions. Not so you walk out with one answer — so the next time the question comes up, you know how to answer it yourself.

Real numbers from real books, read out loud — like reading tea leaves, except it's math. For owners, buyers, and the people who advise them. No accounting background required.
